title: Long-running agent
subtitle: A runnable Long-Running Agent
description: A credit-line-increase agent whose first tool submits a request to a credit bureau and then genuinely waits - potentially hours or days in reality - for the bureau's asynchronous reply, correlated via an inbound webhook, with zero engine resources consumed while it waits. An engine-native timer, scoped precisely to that one wait, tells the agent if the bureau's SLA elapses; the agent then decides for itself whether to hand the case to a different team (underwriting ops) for a manual decision.
creator: Camunda
thumbnailAlt: BPMN model: a start form feeding a Credit Review Agent ad-hoc subprocess whose tools are a request-then-wait chain (an HTTP call followed by a webhook-backed wait task with its own SLA timer) and an agent-invoked escalation to underwriting ops, both flowing into a shared customer notification step.
